summary.tldr: Creates a new court order for domestic violence fears and changes bail, conditions, and evidence rules in related Criminal Code cases.
what_it_does: Tightens bail rules for people accused of violence against an intimate partner if they were previously convicted or discharged for violence against an intimate partner.
Requires a justice who makes a release order to ask the prosecutor whether victims were told they can request a copy of the order.
Creates a new recognizance order, a court order to keep the peace, when someone has reasonable grounds to fear domestic violence against an intimate partner or child.
Lets judges add conditions to that order, including treatment programs, no contact rules, travel limits, no-go zones, electronic monitoring, substance bans, and firearm or weapon bans.
Limits how bodily-substance samples and test results can be used, shared, and destroyed, and updates the related court forms.
Makes youth courts handle these orders for young people and require judges to consider Indigenous support services in some cases.
who_it_affects: People accused of intimate partner violence
summary.background: The bill adds a new Criminal Code recognizance for fear of domestic violence. It also changes related Criminal Code rules, youth justice rules, and standard court forms.
